title: moe-proxy refuses to bridge to a daemon whose /health reports another project
description:
Split from task-e7f4026a (HIGH, human-reported, recurring). That row keeps the moe-agent.sh/.ps1 pre-flight slice and the final verification of all three slices, and it dependsOn this task.

Objective: moe-proxy checks which project the daemon it is about to bridge actually serves.
- Today readDaemonInfoResult (packages/moe-proxy/src/utils.ts) compares only the projectPath written in .moe/daemon.json with its own project. A stale file always matches, so after a project's daemon dies, the proxy bridges to whatever daemon now holds that port.
- On 2026-10-30 a px4swarm seat registered with the moes daemon this way, then claimed and coded a moes task.
- Every wrapper RPC also goes through this proxy: moe_rpc and Invoke-MoeRpc spawn it one-shot. So this check alone stops a seat from registering or claiming on a foreign daemon.

Deliverable:
- A new packages/moe-proxy/src/daemonIdentity.ts.
  - It GETs http://<getDaemonHost()>:<port>/health with a bounded timeout and a body capped at 64 KiB.
  - It classifies the reply as same, foreign (with the served projectPath) or unknown.
  - It compares paths with comparableProjectPath from utils.ts, the rule the daemon's own probeDaemonHealth uses (D:\x == D:/x == /mnt/d/x).
  - It imports utils.ts but does not edit it: task-a4ad3fdb and task-724e31fa edit that file.
- packages/moe-proxy/src/index.ts connect() runs the probe before it opens /mcp, on every connect and reconnect.
  - Foreign: write an error naming both projects and the fix, then exit 1. That is the same class as today's 'daemon.json belongs to a different project'. The fix is: this project's .moe/daemon.json is stale; restart this project's daemon, which takes the next free port. The proxy never opens /mcp.
  - Unknown: proceed exactly as today, so the reconnect path and older daemons keep working. Unknown covers an unreachable /health, a timeout, a non-JSON or oversize body, and a reply with no projectPath from an older daemon.
- Tests:
  - packages/moe-proxy/src/daemonIdentity.test.ts, against a real local http server;
  - one end-to-end case that spawns the proxy against a fake daemon whose /health names another project, and asserts exit 1, the message, and that no /mcp upgrade arrived.

Not in scope:
- daemon code: there is no wire change, and a project parameter on the upgrade is deferred hardening;
- moe-agent.sh/.ps1 (task-e7f4026a);
- the JetBrains plugin (a sibling task);
- the proxy README and utils.ts.

Verification command (fresh, exit 0): cd packages/moe-proxy && npm test. From WSL, run it in a Linux-native snapshot, because the checkout's node_modules are Windows builds (mem:gotcha-daemon-linux-snapshot-gate).
definitionOfDone: connect() probes the daemon's /health before opening /mcp, on every connect and reconnect. When the reply's projectPath is another project by comparableProjectPath, the proxy exits 1 with an error naming both projects and telling the reader to restart this project's daemon, and it makes no /mcp upgrade. Proven by an end-to-end test against a fake daemon.

This project spelled D:\x, D:/x or /mnt/d/x connects as before. An unreachable /health, a timeout, a non-JSON or oversize body, and a reply without projectPath all keep today's behavior. Proven by daemonIdentity.test.ts rows.
packages/moe-proxy/src/utils.ts is unchanged; the diff is daemonIdentity.ts, its tests and index.ts.
`cd packages/moe-proxy && npm test` exits 0, with its output supplied to complete_task.

amendments.reason: Aligns with the classification rule fixed for the JetBrains sibling (task-90664db1; planner note comment-927340a6). The daemon's /health returns 503 when unhealthy and reports the raw --project argument (packages/moe-daemon/src/index.ts ~:61 and ~:703), which can be relative. A 503 carrying an absolute, different projectPath is foreign; a relative projectPath is unknown.

implementationPlan.description:
Create packages/moe-proxy/src/daemonIdentity.ts.

Exports:
- `export type DaemonIdentity = { kind: 'same' } | { kind: 'foreign'; projectPath: string } | { kind: 'unknown' };`
- `export async function probeDaemonIdentity(host: string, port: number, projectPath: string, options: { timeoutMs?: number } = {}): Promise<DaemonIdentity>`. The default timeoutMs is 1500, a named const; /health is local and answers in milliseconds.
- `export const MAX_HEALTH_BODY_BYTES = 64 * 1024`.

Behavior:
- One node:http GET of http://<host>:<port>/health, with a hostname option; a bare IPv6 literal works without brackets.
- One overall timer that destroys the request, plus the request's own timeout.
- Byte-counted reads: destroy and answer unknown once the total exceeds MAX_HEALTH_BODY_BYTES.
- Settle exactly once, through a `done` guard.
- Answer:
  - statusCode 200, a JSON object (not an array), and a non-empty string projectPath: 'same' when comparableProjectPath(reply) === comparableProjectPath(projectPath), else {kind:'foreign', projectPath: reply};
  - everything else is 'unknown'.
- Never reject. Every error, timeout or parse failure resolves {kind:'unknown'}.
- Clear the timer and destroy the socket on every path. Import comparableProjectPath from './utils.js', and do NOT edit utils.ts: task-a4ad3fdb and task-724e31fa edit it.

Add a header comment on why the probe exists. A stale daemon.json always matches its own project, so a port reused by another project's daemon would be bridged (task-e7f4026a). Unknown keeps today's behavior for older daemons and the reconnect path.

Run daemonIdentity.test.ts group A green.
implementationPlan.note: Created daemonIdentity.ts per amend-1: probeDaemonIdentity, DaemonIdentity, MAX_HEALTH_BODY_BYTES, isAbsoluteAnyOs; accepts 200/503 only, relative projectPath -> unknown, one done-guarded settle, overall timer + request timeout + 64 KiB byte cap. Also amended step-1 tests (503-same row, sub/proj row, isAbsoluteAnyOs rows) and fixed a test bug (WebSocketServer address() read before 'listening'). Group A green in snapshot: 41 passed; E1/E3 still red until step 3 (index.ts unchanged), E2/E4 pass.

amendments.description:
Create packages/moe-proxy/src/daemonIdentity.ts.

Exports:
- `export type DaemonIdentity = { kind: 'same' } | { kind: 'foreign'; projectPath: string } | { kind: 'unknown' };`
- `export async function probeDaemonIdentity(host: string, port: number, projectPath: string, options: { timeoutMs?: number } = {}): Promise<DaemonIdentity>`. The default timeoutMs is 1500, a named const; /health is local and answers in milliseconds.
- `export const MAX_HEALTH_BODY_BYTES = 64 * 1024`.

Behavior:
- One node:http GET of http://<host>:<port>/health, using the hostname option, so a bare IPv6 literal works without brackets.
- One overall timer that destroys the request, plus the request's own timeout.
- Count bytes as they are read. Once the total exceeds MAX_HEALTH_BODY_BYTES, destroy the request and answer unknown.
- Settle exactly once, through a `done` guard.

Classification, shared with JetBrains task-90664db1:
- Accept only statusCode 200 or 503 (the daemon's healthy and unhealthy /health codes).
- The body must parse as a JSON object, not an array.
- projectPath must be a non-empty ABSOLUTE string: a drive letter (/^[a-zA-Z]:[\\/]/), UNC (starting with two backslashes) or POSIX (starting with '/'). Write it as a small exported isAbsoluteAnyOs(), not path.isAbsolute, which on Linux rejects 'D:\\x'.
- Then: 'same' when comparableProjectPath(reply) === comparableProjectPath(projectPath), else {kind:'foreign', projectPath: reply}.
- Everything else is 'unknown': a relative projectPath (the daemon reports its raw --project argument), any other status, and any error, timeout or parse failure.

Never reject. Clear the timer and destroy the socket on every path. Import comparableProjectPath from './utils.js', and do NOT edit utils.ts (task-a4ad3fdb and task-724e31fa edit it).

Header comment: why the probe exists. A stale daemon.json always matches its own project, so a port reused by another project's daemon would be bridged (task-e7f4026a). 'unknown' keeps today's behavior for older daemons and for the reconnect path.

Run daemonIdentity.test.ts group A until it is green.
amendments.reason: This step adopts the shared classification rule: 200 or 503 with an absolute projectPath; a relative path or any other status is unknown. That keeps the proxy and the JetBrains sibling (task-90664db1) identical. Without it, an unhealthy foreign daemon (503) would be bridged, and a relative --project could be misread as foreign.

implementationPlan.description:
packages/moe-proxy/src/index.ts, connect() (~:366): probe before opening /mcp, on every connect and reconnect, since both go through connect().

- Keep the daemon.json branch exactly as it is (missing, retryable, non-retryable).
- Move the existing socket code, from `closeWebSocket();` through the ws handler wiring, unchanged into `function openDaemonSocket(projectPath: string, port: number): void`.
- After `info` is known, call `probeDaemonIdentity(getDaemonHost(), info.port, projectPath).then(identity => { ... })`:
  - If `shuttingDown` is set, return without opening a socket; gracefulShutdown owns the exit.
  - foreign: writeError(...) with a message naming both projects and the fix, then process.exit(1). Suggested message: `Daemon on port <port> serves project <identity.projectPath>, not <projectPath>: this project's .moe/daemon.json is stale. Restart this project's Moe daemon (it takes the next free port).` Also writeLog the same line to stderr.
  - otherwise ('same' or 'unknown'): openDaemonSocket(projectPath, info.port).
- The probe never rejects, so add no .catch that could open a second socket.
- Messages arriving during the probe queue in pendingMessages, as they do while disconnected today (isConnected is false). Do not change that queueing, the reconnect window or the timeout checker.

Import probeDaemonIdentity from './daemonIdentity.js'. utils.ts stays unchanged.

Error handling: a foreign daemon is fatal and non-retryable, the same class as 'daemon.json belongs to a different project'. 'unknown' is never fatal.
implementationPlan.note: connect() now probes /health after readDaemonInfoResult and before any /mcp socket; the old socket+stdin code is moved verbatim into openDaemonSocket(projectPath, port). Foreign: writeLog+writeError (both projects + 'Restart this project's Moe daemon') then exit 1; unknown/same: openDaemonSocket; shuttingDown during the probe: return. Deviation from plan wording, deliberate: the stdin reader stays inside openDaemonSocket (runs after the probe) rather than before it. Reason: wrapper RPCs write a request then close stdin; if stdin were live during the probe, gracefulShutdown would set shuttingDown with the message queued and the shuttingDown guard would then skip opening /mcp, stranding the request. Added a .catch that mirrors main().catch (writeError + exit 1) so a sync throw in openDaemonSocket is not an unhandled rejection; it cannot open a second socket. Test message assertion made case-insensitive (/restart/i). Full proxy suite in snapshot: 6 files, 223 tests passed.

implementationPlan.description:
ADVERSARIAL SELF-REVIEW, once, as the final step. Load adversarial-self-review.

Check:
- Can the probe hang connect()? Look at the overall timer, a black-holed host via MOE_DAEMON_HOST, and a server that trickles bytes forever: the byte cap plus the overall timer must both bound it.
- Can it double-settle or leak a socket or timer?

implementationPlan.note: Adversarial review of the 3-path diff. ONE real finding, fixed: the foreign-daemon message embedded the served projectPath verbatim; it comes from whatever answered the port (up to 64 KiB, may carry newlines), so it could forge stderr log lines or produce a huge error. Added displayServedPath (control chars -> '?', cap 300 chars + '...') used by index.ts; tests: 3 unit rows + E1b e2e; mutant dropping it is killed by E1b alone. Re-ran step 4 fresh after the fix: new snapshot /tmp/moe-proxy-gate.55jUhg, npm test exit 0, 6 files / 237 tests, cmp of the 3 owned files identical. Checked and found sound: (1) hang: overall timer + request timeout + 64 KiB byte cap bound a black-holed host and a trickling server (unit row 'trickles forever' resolves in ~300ms); (2) double-settle/leak: single done guard, timer cleared and req destroyed in finish() on every path, sync http.request throw is caught; (3) shutdown during the probe: guard returns without opening /mcp, equivalent to the cleared reconnect timer, and on first connect stdin is not yet live so only signals can set it; (4) reconnect race: connect() is re-armed only by the close handler or the daemon-missing branch, each single-shot, stale-socket close events are ignored, so one connect never opens two sockets; (5) false foreign: D:\x/D:/x//mnt/d/x, trailing slash and case all go through comparableProjectPath; relative served paths are unknown; UNC-vs-WSL is already refused by the existing daemon.json check; (6) older daemon without projectPath and 426 mocks still connect (E4, index.test.ts); (7) message names only the two paths and the port. executionContract.intendedBehavior: Before every /mcp connect and reconnect, moe-proxy GETs the daemon's /health. When the reply's projectPath is another project by comparableProjectPath, the proxy writes a JSON-RPC error naming both projects and telling the reader to restart this project's daemon, exits 1, and never opens /mcp. A same-project reply, and every unknown outcome (unreachable, timeout, non-JSON, oversize, non-200, or no projectPath), keep today's behavior.
acceptanceCriteria: E1: against a fake daemon whose /health names another project, the proxy exits 1 with the message and makes no /mcp upgrade.
The spelling rows (D:\x, D:/x and /mnt/d/x) classify as same, and every unknown row resolves 'unknown' without rejecting.
The existing index.test.ts e2e cases still pass, and utils.ts is unchanged.
invariants: The probe never rejects, settles once, and is bounded by the timeout and the 64 KiB body cap.
No /mcp socket opens after shutdown starts or for a foreign daemon, and a single connect never opens two sockets.
No daemon or wire change, and no edits to utils.ts, the README or the wrappers.
compatibility: Daemons whose /health lacks projectPath, or whose /health is unreachable, connect as today.
The 'daemon.json belongs to a different project' path and its message are unchanged.
approvedScope: packages/moe-proxy/src/index.ts: connect() probes, then calls openDaemonSocket (the existing socket code, moved unchanged).
reuse: comparableProjectPath and getDaemonHost from utils.ts; index.test.ts's spawn-the-built-proxy harness pattern.
sourceAssumptions: packages/moe-proxy/src/index.ts connect() (~:366) builds ws://<getDaemonHost()>:<port>/mcp after readDaemonInfoResult. Reconnect timers call connect() again.
packages/moe-daemon/src/index.ts /health returns {status, version, pid, uptime, projectPath, stats, checks}.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
- Probe /health in the proxy before opening /mcp (chosen; it is what the task describes). It needs no daemon wire change, because /health already reports projectPath (index.ts startDaemon /health handler).
- Comparing daemon.json's pid with /health's pid: rejected. A stale file names a dead pid while another daemon serves the port; the projectPath answer is what identifies the project.
- Treating unknown as fatal: rejected. Older daemons and transient /health failures must keep today's behavior, and the reconnect path relies on it.
- Editing utils.ts: forbidden, because task-a4ad3fdb and task-724e31fa edit it. Import comparableProjectPath instead.
- Putting the e2e case in index.test.ts: rejected. It goes in daemonIdentity.test.ts so the diff stays at the three files DoD 3 names.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
- index.ts connect() (~:366) is synchronous today: readDaemonInfoResult, then closeWebSocket() and new WebSocket(ws://<getDaemonHost()>:<port>/mcp) with handlers. Reconnects re-enter connect() through a timer that the close handler clears.
- pendingMessages queues stdin messages while isConnected is false (~:602). shuttingDown (~:54) is set by gracefulShutdown.
- writeError writes a JSON-RPC error to stdout; writeLog writes to stderr.
- utils.ts comparableProjectPath maps D:\x, D:/x and /mnt/d/x to 'd:/x' on every OS.
- package.json has pretest = build, so e2e tests spawn a fresh dist/index.js.
- A bare ws WebSocketServer({port}) answers a plain GET with 426, so the existing index.test.ts mocks resolve to 'unknown' and keep passing.
- workerType.integration.test.ts imports daemon source, so the WSL snapshot needs npm ci in both packages.
planningNotes.risks:
- The async gap in connect(): handle shutdown during the probe, never open two sockets, and keep queued messages flowing after open.
- Cross-OS paths: the tests use comparableProjectPath spellings that hold on win32, linux and darwin, because CI runs a 3-OS matrix.
- Windows-native node_modules: the gate must run in a Linux snapshot with both packages installed.
- Sibling rows task-90664db1 (JetBrains) and task-e7f4026a (wrappers plus final verification) depend on this one. Keep the message and the rules stable for them.
